Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cdtr (development version)

This development version collects what will be released as cdtr 0.2.0.

  • cdt_locate(barycentric = TRUE) also returns the barycentric coordinates of each point in its triangle (b1, b2, b3, in the order of T), the weights that interpolate any per-vertex value.

  • New cdt_winding() finds the winding number of each input feature in every triangle by walking the mesh and using edge_sources, with no point-in-polygon step. It is the coverage of each triangle by overlapping inputs, which depth cannot give, and is unaffected by refinement.

  • New cdt_quality() returns per-triangle area, minimum and maximum angle, shortest and longest edge, and radius-edge ratio, to check a mesh or that refinement met its targets.

  • cdt_triangulate(holes = ) takes hole points (a two-column matrix, or a list or data frame with x and y) and erases the region around each that is bounded by constraint segments, as the H of an RTriangle::pslg() does. cdt_pslg() uses p$H when present. This makes a drop-in replacement for Triangle’s holes where polygons are given as rings of segments. A hole point in no bounded region erases nothing.

  • New vignette “Overlapping inputs and edge_sources”: triangulate several overlapping polygons at once and find which inputs cover each triangle by walking the mesh with edge_sources, checked against point-in-polygon.

  • New vignette “A terrain surface from contour lines”, rebuilding a surface around kunanyi (Mount Wellington) from contours with cdt_triangulate_attr() and checking it against the elevation model. The small data file in inst/extdata is from the Tasmania 2 m DEM, The LIST, (c) State of Tasmania, CC BY 3.0 AU (see inst/COPYRIGHTS). It relates the quality of the triangles to the error and appearance of the surface, with a figure.

  • Two vignettes: “Getting started with cdtr” (depth, erase, refinement, crossings, edge_sources, locating and interpolating) and “Polygons, triangle pools and wkpool”.

  • wkpool 0.5.0 uses cdtr (in Suggests) for the constrained triangulation behind tri_overlay() and tri_overlay_relate(), and the output of cdt_pslg() feeds wkpool::new_wkpool_tri(). The polygon vignette shows the route; use erase = "holes" so hole triangles are dropped. polymer builds on both packages.

  • New cdt_locate() returns the triangle containing each query point (NA outside), using the grid of triangle buckets from cdt_interpolate() and exact orientation tests; ties on shared edges go to the lowest triangle. With a triangle-to-feature table this is point-in-polygon for many points. The grid is now one shared, flat structure (src/grid.h) used by both.

  • The development version number (0.1.0.9000 and up) lets packages using edge_sources (polymer) require it.

  • cdt_triangulate(edge_sources = TRUE) returns edge_sources, one row per fixed edge and covering input segment (edge, segment, forward), tracked through crossings, splits and refinement. This is the constraint-to-input map of the mesh spec, and lets callers label regions by which inputs cover them (winding per input), which depth cannot do. An input segment lying on a longer collinear input is no longer lost from CDT’s provenance when refinement splits the shared edge.

  • DESCRIPTION reference now uses the CRAN form Author (year) <doi:...>.

cdtr 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-21

  • First release.
  • cdt_triangulate() wraps the ‘CDT’ C++ library for constrained and conforming Delaunay triangulation, with Ruppert refinement by maximum area or minimum angle, resolution of crossing constraints, and per-triangle topological region depth.
  • Triangles are returned wound counter-clockwise (positive signed area).
  • origin records each vertex’s provenance (input, crossing or steiner).
  • Optional depth_distinct counts a doubled boundary once rather than per copy.
  • Helpers: cdt_pslg(), cdt_triangulate_attr(), cdt_interpolate(), cdt_edges() and default_min_edge_length().
